title: NISM Mutual Fund Distributor (Series V-A)
blurb: Exam prep for NISM-Series-V-A: fund structure, SEBI rules, scheme types, NAV and costs, risk and return measures, planning, tax and conduct.

rows: Anyone preparing for the NISM-Series-V-A certification needed to get an ARN or EUIN
About 136 minutes of lessons, then cards, checkpoints and the final quiz
None. Module 1 (MF Distributor) is useful practice for the client conversation side
22 short lessons in 5 stages, each ending with three exam-style checks
outcomes: Explain the structure of a mutual fund and the role of each constituent.
Name the SEBI scheme categories and match them to client needs.
Calculate NAV, expense effects and basic return and risk measures.
Handle purchase, redemption, SIP, STP, SWP and cut-off rules correctly.
Apply the AMFI code of conduct and the complaint route.

sources: SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996 and the SEBI Master Circular for Mutual Funds (check the current edition)
SEBI circular on categorisation and rationalisation of mutual fund schemes (October 2017) and later changes
NISM-Series-V-A: Mutual Fund Distributors Certification Examination workbook (current edition)
AMFI Code of Conduct for intermediaries; AMFI registration (ARN, EUIN) guidelines
Income-tax Act provisions for mutual funds: rates change often, verify before advising
Practice exam only: confirm the current NISM exam format, marks and pass mark before booking

syllabus.topic: Concept and role of mutual funds
Distribution, commissions and AMFI code of conduct

lessons.title: Concept and role of mutual funds
Fund structure and constituents
Fund governance, accounting and portfolio disclosures
Regulatory framework and unitholder rights
Market basics for fund investors: equity, debt instruments and indices
Scheme types and the SEBI categories
Equity and hybrid scheme categories
Debt and liquid scheme categories
ETFs, index funds, fund of funds and international funds
NFOs and offer documents: SID, SAI and KIM
Specialised Investment Funds and other newer products
NAV, valuation, expenses and loads
Transactions: purchase, redemption, cut-offs, SIP, STP and SWP
KYC, folio, nomination and investor services
Measuring returns
Measuring risk and risk-adjusted return
Scheme selection and model portfolios
Financial planning basics
Taxation of mutual funds
Distribution channels, commissions and disclosures
Distributor registration, AMFI code of conduct and ethics
Complaints, grievance redressal and a mock case lab

cards.q: Name the core benefits of a mutual fund.
a: Regulation and transparency. Market risk remains.
AMFI: industry body, ARN and code.
Multi cap 25% each in three buckets.
Side pocket isolates a defaulted paper.
ETF on exchange, index fund at NAV.
Sharpe: per unit of total risk (SD).
Treynor: per unit of market risk (beta).
Then the schemes, checked for cost and overlap.
ARN: AMFI registration of the distributor.

final.title: NISM Mutual Fund Distributor (Series V-A) final quiz

questions.q: Investors in a mutual fund hold:
questions.why: Investors own units of the scheme in proportion to their investment.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of a mutual fund?
questions.why: Professional management and diversification are core benefits.

questions.q: Which entity holds the securities of a scheme?
questions.why: An independent custodian holds the securities.

questions.q: Who appoints the AMC?
questions.why: The trustees appoint the AMC with SEBI approval.

questions.q: Who safekeeps the scheme's securities?
questions.why: The custodian holds the securities.

questions.q: Assets 1,050, liabilities 10, units 100 crore. NAV is:
The regulator of mutual funds in India is:
questions.why: SEBI regulates mutual funds.

questions.q: A change in fundamental attributes gives unitholders:
o: An exit option without exit load
questions.why: Unitholders get an exit option at NAV with no load.

questions.q: Treasury bills are issued at:
questions.why: T-bills are zero-coupon and discounted.

questions.q: The highest credit rating category is:
questions.why: AAA is the highest; D is default.

questions.q: Units of a closed-ended scheme are usually:
questions.why: Closed-ended units are listed (or repurchase offers are made).

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the five SEBI scheme groups?
questions.why: The five groups are equity, debt, hybrid, solution-oriented and other.

questions.q: A large-cap fund must invest at least what share in large caps?
questions.why: At least 80% of assets go to the top 100 companies.

questions.q: A focused fund may hold at most:
questions.why: SEBI caps focused funds at 30 stocks.

questions.q: A liquid fund invests in securities maturing up to:
questions.why: Liquid funds hold papers up to 91 days.

questions.q: A gilt fund invests at least 80% in:
questions.why: Gilt funds buy government securities.

questions.q: Which product is bought and sold on a stock exchange?
questions.why: ETFs trade on the exchange.

questions.q: Tracking error measures:
o: Volatility of the gap between fund and index returns
questions.why: It is the standard deviation of the return difference.

questions.q: The document with scheme-specific details is the:
questions.why: The SID holds scheme-specific information.

questions.q: The maximum period an NFO can stay open is:
questions.why: An NFO can be open for at most 15 days.

questions.q: An FMP is generally:
questions.why: FMPs are closed-ended.

questions.q: A segregated portfolio is used to:
o: Isolate a defaulted or downgraded security
questions.why: It side-pockets stressed paper.

questions.q: Assets ₹300 crore, liabilities ₹10 crore, units 29 crore. NAV is:
Entry load was abolished in:
questions.why: SEBI banned entry load from August 2009.

questions.q: The normal cut-off for equity fund purchase is:
questions.why: Most purchase and redemption cut-offs are 3:00 pm.

questions.q: An STP transfers money:
o: From one scheme to another within the same AMC
From a bank to a broker
questions.why: STP moves a fixed amount between schemes of the same AMC.

questions.q: A folio is:
o: An investor's account with an AMC
questions.why: A folio is the investor's account number with an AMC.

questions.q: A CAS shows:
questions.why: A consolidated account statement covers multiple AMCs.

questions.q: For a SIP with many cash flows, the best return measure is:
questions.why: XIRR handles irregular dates and amounts.

questions.q: ₹1,000 becomes ₹1,210 in two years. CAGR is:
Sharpe ratio divides excess return by:
questions.why: Sharpe = (return − risk-free) ÷ standard deviation.

questions.q: A beta of 1.3 means the fund is:
questions.why: Beta above 1 means a more volatile fund.

questions.q: Which scheme suits parking money for 3 months?
questions.why: Short horizons need low-volatility, high-liquidity funds.

questions.q: The first step in scheme selection is:
questions.why: Goal, horizon and risk come first.

questions.q: By the rule of 72, money at 12% doubles in about:
An equity-oriented fund holds at least what share in domestic equity?
questions.why: At least 65% in domestic equity makes it equity-oriented for tax.

questions.q: Trail commission is paid out of:
questions.why: Trail comes from the scheme's expense ratio.

questions.q: EUIN stands for:
questions.why: EUIN identifies the individual who sold the product.

questions.q: The online SEBI platform for investor complaints is:
questions.why: SCORES is SEBI's complaint redress system.
